author: product-requirements-expert
context: Fresh feature dispatch: staff cancel a wrongly booked visit from the owner detail page. Scoping it into a prd-entry stops at the PRD Non-Goals table, which declines this feature by name in two rows. NG-5 declines 'Changing or cancelling a visit once booked' (rationale: amendment would add lifecycle state the sample deliberately has none of). NG-4 declines 'Deleting an owner, a pet, or a visit'. The request's 'cancelling removes that visit from the pet's record' lands on both. The Visits section (REQ-VIS-001, REQ-VIS-002) holds no cancellation behavior to refine, so this is a new requirement, minted as REQ-VIS-003. Note: my dispatch-start at line 1 carries REQ-VIS-002 in error, composed before reading the PRD where that ID already means 'earlier visits shown when booking'; line 2 re-anchors under REQ-VIS-003. Two further facts bearing on your decision: the demonstration framing confirmed 2026-07-31 (G-1) is the stated reason behind every Non-Goals row, so a reversal here is a scope decision about what the sample teaches; and the owner detail page today lists a pet's visits with no past/future distinction, so 'upcoming' introduces a distinction the record does not currently make.
question: Three decisions, all yours. (1) Do you override NG-4 and NG-5 to admit visit cancellation? A yes narrows both rows rather than deleting them: NG-4 would continue to decline deleting an owner or a pet, NG-5 would continue to decline changing a booked visit's date or description. If you instead want correction-by-amendment (fix the wrong pet or wrong day in place) rather than cancellation, say so now, because that is a different requirement. (2) Which visits offer the action? Proposed default: a visit dated later than today, reusing the boundary REQ-VIS-001 already sets for booking, so a visit offers cancel exactly while it could still have been booked. Consequence worth your attention: your stated problem includes 'wrong pet', and a mis-booking noticed after the date has passed would stay on the record uncorrectable. Alternatives are today-or-later, or every visit regardless of date. (3) Does 'removes that visit from the pet's record' mean the visit is gone from every view of that pet, with nothing retained? Proposed default: yes, gone, leaving no trace. If the clinic needs to see that a visit was cancelled, that is a retained-history requirement and I will write it as one.
stop_state: Nothing written to docs/prd.md or docs/ubiquitous-language.md: the change reverses recorded decisions, so I stopped before drafting. On your answers I add REQ-VIS-003 to the Visits section with its Done-when bullets and edge cases, narrow the NG-4 and NG-5 rows, write docs/adr/2026-08-05-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md recording the reversal, add cancellation vocabulary to docs/ubiquitous-language.md (the Visit entry carries no lifecycle terms today), and append the prd-entry.
